items.originalTitle: Disney Plus, Hulu, and HBO Max are all over 50 percent off for Black Friday
items.author: Sheena Vasani
items.title: Disney Plus, Hulu, and HBO Max are all over 50 percent off for Black Friday
items.summary: HBO’s A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms takes a surprisingly charming approach to Westerosi medievalism. | Image: HBO Black Friday isn’t just a good time to save on a new TV but also a chance to spend less on what you watch on it. The shopping holiday often brings steep streaming discounts, and this year is no exception, with some streamers offering more than 50 percent off. HBO Max, Apple TV, and Hulu are all offering deals, with several plans going for just a few dollars a month. Some discounts even apply to ad-free plans, though there are fewer than last year and prices are generally higher. Still, you can save big if you don’t mind a few commercials. Right now, for example, you can get a year of the ad-supported Disney Plus and Hulu bundle for $4.99 a month, saving you $96, or sign up for the most basic HBO Max plan for $5.49 a month for 12 months, saving you $66. We’ve rounded up these deals and more below, including what each plan offers and how long you can take advantage of the discounted rate. Disney Plus and Hulu Disney Plus, Hulu Bundle Where to Buy: $12.99 $4.99 at Hulu (ad-supported, monthly) $21.99 $14.99 at Hulu (ad-free, monthly) With everything from Disney classics and Marvel movies to FX dramas like The Bear and Shōgun , the Disney Plus and Hulu bundle offers plenty for the whole family to watch. For Black Friday, you can get both services with ads for just $4.99 per month ($8 off) for a year via Hulu or Disney Plus , saving you $96 in total. The ad-free bundle is also on sale for $14.99 per month ($7 off) for 12 months, saving you $84. Both discounts are available through 11:59PM PT on November 30th. Whichever plan you choose, you’ll get access to both streaming libraries. Hulu offers dramas like Furious , Alien: Earth , The Lowdown , and The Handmaid’s Tale , as well as comedies like Bob’s Burgers , Futurama , and It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia . Disney Plus, meanwhile, is home to Disney and Pixar favorites, The Simpsons , and a wide selection of Star Wars and Marvel movies and shows. It’s also a good option for holiday movie nights, with classics like Home Alone and The Santa Clause . HBO Max HBO Max Where to Buy: $10.49 $5.49 at Amazon (monthly, with ads) $10.99 $5.49 at HBO Max (monthly, with ads) HBO Max is home to some of Hollywood’s biggest releases, and right now, you can watch them for half the usual rate. Now through November 30th, new and returning subscribers can sign up for HBO Max’s Basic With Ads plan for $5.49 a month via HBO Max or Amazon , saving you $66 over the course of a year. Although the plan doesn’t include live sports, it supports simultaneous streaming on two devices and gives you access to everything from award-winning films like Sinners and Marty Supreme to Wuthering Heights . There’s arguably even more to watch on the TV front, from dramas like The Gilded Age , Lanterns , Euphoria , and Heated Rivalry to comedies such as Hacks and The Righteous Gemstones . Fantasy fans, meanwhile, can immerse themselves in the world of Game of Thrones and its spinoffs, including House of the Dragon and A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms , or check out Dune: Prophecy . You’ll also be able to stream new releases, including HBO’s upcoming Harry Potter series . Peacock Peacock Where to Buy: $8.99 $2.99 at Peacock (monthly, Select) $12.99 $8.99 at Peacock (monthly, Premium) $89.99 $29.99 at Peacock (annual, Select) If you’re looking for an affordable way to catch up on NBC shows, Peacock’s Black Friday promotion offers two ways to save. Through November 30th, new and returning subscribers can sign up for Peacock Select for $2.99 a month ($6 off) for three months or $29.99 ($60 off) for a full year . For access to Peacock’s larger catalog, you can also subscribe to Peacock Premium for $8.99 per month for three months or $89.99 ($40 off) for a year. The cheaper Select tier is a particularly good value if you mainly watch shows from networks like NBC, Bravo, and Telemundo, including Saturday Night Live , The Office , and Below Deck . Movie buffs and sports fans, however, will prefer Premium, which offers access to a much wider selection of entertainment. Peacock’s catalog includes films like The Super Mario Galaxy Movie , Disclosure Day , and Minions & Monsters , along with shows like The Good Daughter , Dig , and The Paper . A Premium subscription also lets you watch live sporting events, including Sunday Night Football , as well as Peacock originals, such as the various Love Island spinoffs. Paramount Plus Paramount Plus (monthly subscription) Where to Buy: $8.99 $2.99 at Paramount (Essential) $13.99 $2.99 at Paramount (Premium) If you’re a Star Trek fan or want another way to watch live sports, Paramount Plus is down to $2.99 per month for two months for Black Friday. New and eligible returning subscribers can take advantage of the discount through November 30th, bringing the cost of both the Essential and Premium plans to $5.98 for the introductory period. That makes Premium a particularly good deal, since it normally costs $13.99 a month, compared to $8.99 for the ad-supported Essential tier. Paramount Plus includes CBS shows like NCIS and Everybody Loves Raymond to Tulsa King and the various Yellowstone spinoffs, including both 1883 and 1923 . Movie fans can also browse Paramount’s film library, which includes titles like Arrival , Top Gun , and Interstellar , while sports fans can watch select NFL games, UFC events, UEFA Champions League matches, and March Madness games. Premium also grants you access to Showtime originals and a live feed of your local CBS station, along with ad-free on-demand viewing, though live programming still includes commercials. Apple TV Apple TV (six-month subscription) Where to Buy: $15 $7 at Amazon (monthly) Apple TV has built an impressive collection of acclaimed shows, particularly if you’re into sci-fi shows like Silo or thrillers like Slow Horses . Right now, US customers with an Amazon account can subscribe to Apple TV through Amazon for $6.99 per month ($8 off) for six months , saving $48 over the introductory period. Amazon hasn’t listed an end date for the promotion, either. Six months should give you plenty of time to work through Apple’s other originals, including Severance , Pachinko , The Morning Show , and Pluribus , or settle in for a movie like Arrival or Anchorman . The service also includes live sports, specifically Formula 1 races and Major League Soccer matches. Crunchyroll Crunchyroll Where to Buy: $9.99 $3.99 at Crunchyroll (Fan) $13.99 $5.99 at Crunchyroll (Mega fan) $17.99 $8.99 at Crunchyroll (Ultimate fan) Anime fans can spend the next six months catching up on shows like The Apothecary Diaries , Jujutsu Kaisen , Black Clover , and One Piece for a lot less thanks to Crunchyroll’s Black Friday sale . Select new and returning subscribers in the US can sign up for the Fan plan for $3.99 a month ($6 off) for six months, saving them $36. The Mega Fan tier is also down to $5.99 a month ($8 off) for six months, while Ultimate Fan is available for $8.99 a month ($9 off) for the same period. Amazon is also offering the same discount on the Mega Fan tier . All three subscriptions offer access to Crunchyroll’s full anime library without ads, including new episodes shortly after they air in Japan. The Fan tier lets you watch on one device at a time, while Mega Fan increases that limit to four devices and adds offline viewing and access to Crunchyroll’s Game Vault. Ultimate Fan, meanwhile, supports six simultaneous streams and includes Crunchyroll Manga, along with additional store perks. Starz Starz Where to Buy: $69.99 $11.99 at Starz (annual) $10.99 $2.99 at Starz (monthly) If you didn’t get a chance to watch the Michael Jackson biopic Michael when it was released earlier this year or just want to catch up on Outlander , Starz is offering a particularly affordable way to stream both on Black Friday. Eligible subscribers can sign up for a year directly through Starz or Amazon Prime for $11.99 ($58 off), which works out to about $1 a month when you pay upfront. If you’d rather not commit to a year, you can alternatively subscribe for $2.99 per month ($9 off) for three months. Either option lets you explore Starz’s catalog of films and TV shows, including In the Grey , Power Ballad , Splash City , and P-Valley . Other streaming deals of note Amazon is also discounting a wide range of subscriptions through Prime Video , including NBA League Pass, AMC Plus, MGM Plus, and several bundles. Most of the deals below are available through November 30th. Now through December 1st, you can get the standard version of NBA League Pass for $49.99 ($60 off); the Premium tier is also available for $74.99 ($85 off). You can subscribe to AMC Plus Premium for $2.75 per month (about $8 off) for two months through November 30th, or get the ad-free plan for $1.99 per month ($8 off) for two months. MGM Plus is down to $1.99 ($6 off) per month for two months. If you’d like both services, the AMC Plus Premium and MGM Plus bundle is available for $3.49 per month ($10 off) for two months through November 30th. You can also get AMC Plus, MGM Plus, and Starz together for $5.49 per month (about $16 off) for two months. Horror fans can also bundle MGM Plus and horror service Shudder through Prime Video for $12.99 a month ($5 off), down from the usual combined price of $17.98 a month. If you’re planning a holiday movie marathon this weekend, Hallmark Plus is available for $2.25 per month (about $7 off) for three months. You can subscribe to PBS Kids for $1.25 per month (about $4 off) for two months. BritBox , which offers British series like The Other Bennet Sister , is available for $2.75 per month (around $8 off) for two months.

items.originalTitle: Protein redesign boosts DNA insertion activity and reveals how molecular machinery selects targets
items.title: Protein redesign boosts DNA insertion activity and reveals how molecular machinery selects targets
items.summary: Genome engineering is exciting, given its vast potential to treat and even cure diseases, but it is still a largely uncharted biomedical innovation. Scientists at St. Jude Children's Research Hospital recently uncovered the mechanisms involved in precisely integrating DNA into a target genomic location using CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs). By studying type I-F3 CAST, the researchers unveiled structural findings that explain how this CAST family achieves successful DNA integration at precise target sites and offer insights for future genomic engineering approaches. The results were published in Nature.

items.originalTitle: Here’s where you can save (a little) on the Ocarina of Time remake
items.author: Cameron Faulkner
items.title: Here’s where you can save (a little) on the Ocarina of Time remake
items.summary: The Nintendo Switch 2 remake delivers a complete graphical overhaul and numerous quality-of-life updates to the ‘98 classic. | Image: Nintendo A lot of people have The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Nintendo Switch 2 on their holiday wishlist. In case you haven’t bought it yet, I wanted to share some small but welcome deals happening on the physical and digital versions of the game. Costco members can currently grab the cartridge edition for $62.99, down from its regular price of $69.99 (it’s the only retailer currently discounting the physical version). Both Amazon and Costco are also selling the digital version for $54.99, a small $5 discount. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Where to Buy: $59.99 $54.99 at Amazon (Digital) $69.99 $62.99 at Costco (Physical) Ocarina of Time is one of Nintendo’s most groundbreaking titles, having served as its first 3D Zelda game when it launched in 1998. Parts of the original game haven’t aged particularly well — namely some dungeon design and the game’s tricky 3D navigation, since there was only one analog stick at the time — which makes it tough for some to enjoy going back to play the N64 version. Thankfully, the Switch 2 remake introduces several fixes, a host of quality-of-life improvements, and, of course, some lovely visuals that make it a graphics powerhouse by today’s standards. If you go the digital route, a recent Switch 2 update lets you gift games to players in your family group. It doesn’t have to be your actual family, either, just up to eight people you designate as part of your group. The digital game will then appear gift-wrapped on their homescreen. Read our full Ocarina of Time review .

items.originalTitle: China and Brazil Lead Pushback Against Trump’s ‘Unacceptable’ Tariff Threats
items.author: Callum Sutherland and Olivia-Anne Cleary
items.title: China and Brazil Lead Pushback Against Trump’s ‘Unacceptable’ Tariff Threats
items.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump delivers remarks on reciprocal tariffs during an event at the White House on April 2, 2025. —Brendan Smialowski—Getty Images China warned Thursday that it reserves the right to take “necessary measures” to retaliate against the Trump Administration’s proposed new tariffs , which have reignited global trade tensions. “China urges the U.S. to correct its wrong practices and return to the right track of resolving issues through dialogue and consultation,” said He Yadong, spokesperson for the Ministry of Commerce. He added that Beijing “reserves the right to take necessary measures and will resolutely safeguard its legitimate rights and interests.” The Trump Administration targeted 14 trading partners Wednesday in a slew of new tariffs that are set to come into effect early next year. The levies will be imposed under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 following an investigation led by U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer. The U.S. said the probe had found demonstrations of unfair trade practices and excess manufacturing capacity. Mexico and Norway were not listed in the new proposals, as investigations into their respective trade practices are ongoing. Greer framed the tariffs as a way to “level the playing field for American workers and chart a new, more sustainable course for the world economy.” The Section 301 avenue is a way for the Trump Administration to reinstate many of the tariffs that were deemed illegal and struck down by the Supreme Court in February. China is facing a 20% tariff, which the Trump Administration said it could double to 40% if Beijing does not adhere to the terms of an existing trade truce with Washington. Another major U.S. trading partner, Vietnam, is facing tariffs of up to 35%. The country’s Ministry of Industry and Trade said it was in the process of “developing and submitting counter-arguments to the preliminary conclusions and inaccurate opinions and allegations from relevant parties.” The proposed tariffs are subject to a public notice and comment period, with a hearing set to take place early next year before they go into effect, allowing countries to issue responses and arguments. Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Singapore-based Hinrich Foundation, says the proposed measures are already generating significant “resentment” among trading partners. On top of that, the proposed rates have prompted uncertainty for major economies as to what Washington could do next. “If the U.S. unilaterally determines that the partner is not living up to expectations, then the number can ramp up higher,” she says. “That doesn't really support trust, and it makes it very hard to plan ahead.” Amid rising tensions, several trading partners are already following China’s lead in voicing their disapproval over the rates. Bernd Lange, trade committee chair in the European Parliament, said it was “absurd” the E.U. is facing a 20% tariff. He expressed hope that any enforced tariffs will adhere to the Turnberry agreement signed between Washington and the E.U. last year, which capped U.S. tariffs at 15%. “Washington’s allegations about E.U. industrial overcapacity are absurd. We’ll now see whether the announced U.S. tariffs comply with Turnberry in practice,” he said. “If Washington breaches its commitments, the E.U. must act swiftly. It has the legal means to do so.” Elms says the threat to hike rates against economies that already have a trade pact with the U.S. further calls into question “how durable” trade commitments with Washington are. Singapore and Japan also hit back at the prospect of respective 20% tariff rates. Singapore’s Ministry of Energy, Trade, and Industry said it was “very disappointed” by the assessment and argued that the U.S. Trade Representative’s findings “do not take into account the structure of Singapore’s economy.” Japan’s Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara referred to the U.S. tariffs as “regrettable,” insisting that: “Japan does not have any nonmarket policies or practices, or structural excess production capacity in the first place.” Brazil fights back after being singled out Alongside the sweeping tariffs against 14 trading partners, the Trump Administration published a separate proposal seeking to raise levies on Brazil by specifically targeting its sugar and aircraft exports. “Imposing an additional, specific tariff on sugar imports from Brazil and an additional 10% tariff on finished aircraft exports from Brazil is intended to help bring Brazil to the table,” said the office of the USTR (U.S. Trade Representative). The announcement came amid stalled trade talks between Washington and Brazil. The Brazilian government expressed “outrage” over the proposed raising of rates, arguing that it has “been acting in good faith in negotiations” relating to Section 301 with the U.S. for over a year. “The USTR's unilateral decision constitutes an unacceptable action within the ongoing bilateral negotiation process. Brazil will not yield to this type of threat,” the government vowed in a statement. It said Brazil would continue to negotiate with the U.S., “without ruling out the possibility of adopting retaliatory measures in response to the illegal and unjust imposition of tariffs on Brazilian products.” Democratic lawmaker vows to tackle Trump’s tariffs The Trump Administration could face significant pushback from the U.S. Congress next year, as Democrats will take control of both the House and Senate in January following sweeping victories in the midterms. Senator Ron Wyden of Oregon, who will chair the Senate Finance Committee next year, has vowed to try and overturn Trump’s tariffs. “This is another blatant attempt by Donald Trump to reconstruct his illegal global tariffs, no matter the cost to American families, workers, and small businesses. Global overcapacity is a serious problem, but Trump’s unilateral price-hiking tariffs are not the solution,” Wyden said in a statement . “As incoming Finance Committee Chairman, I will use every tool at my disposal to end Trump’s tariff chaos and restore Congress’ constitutional authority over trade.” However, securing a veto-proof majority to rein in Trump’s authority could well prove difficult. Among the general public, tariffs remain deeply unpopular with Americans. An NBC News exit poll following the midterm elections found that 66% of voters believed Trump’s tariff policies had hurt the national economy.

items.summary: X is finally rolling out parental controls that allow parents and guardians to manage teens' accounts on the platform. While teens will retain ownership of their own account, parents and guardians will be able to see how much time their child has spent on X, set daily limits, require approval for new followers, and limit For You recommendations to accounts a teen already follows. "Parents and guardians cannot read private messages, see searches or viewing history, post as their teen, or access the account," explains the X safety team. items.originalTitle: Champions League review: Lille monster Bayern, De Bruyne’s sad return and more United chaos
items.author: John Brewin
items.title: Champions League review: Lille monster Bayern, De Bruyne’s sad return and more United chaos
items.summary: The French side earned their first group win over troubled German giants as Bellingham and Betis also caught the eye Bayern Munich have hit a snagging point, with injuries wracking Vincent Kompany’s squad just as the head coach returns to work following his own health scare. For Lille’s winner, to exact Bayern’s first loss of the season, Aleksandar Pavlović had an own goal for the ages, desperately chasing back to then somehow direct the ball into his own net. Bayern are 15th in the Champions League table, and with Harry Kane out until well into 2027 and 18-year-old Lennart Karl asked to lead the line, resources are stretched. Jamal Musiala, subject of club grandees Uli Hoeness and Karl Heinz-Rummenigge’s gripes over his contract in the light of his neurological condition, could also play only 15 minutes.
